manifest.name: @jjunho/dsh-peer2peer
manifest.description: Local peer-to-peer messaging between DeepSeek Harness sessions over an in-memory bus

bundle.text:
# @jjunho/dsh-peer2peer bundle patch — applied as one insert over the profile root.
#
# The host row registers the six peer_* tools into the `tools` registry and
# holds an in-memory bus in its closure. DSH hosts many sessions in ONE process,
# so two "windows" are two sessions of the same runtime and share that bus
# directly — no sockets, no files, no registry. The bus is not a published
# Cordis service, so the row needs no isolate realm and is safe at either plane:
#
#   • HOST BUNDLE (this file, via `dsh plugin add`): one plugin instance per
#     process, keyed per session internally.
#   • AGENT PRESET (copy the row into `agent.cordis.yml`): identical behavior.
#
# The client "Peer Console" UI ships as source (`client.js`) because its browser
# module must be produced by the deepseek-harness monorepo build (JSX + CSS
# modules). See README for the compilation step; the tools work without it.

- insert:
    - id: peer2peer
      name: '@jjunho/dsh-peer2peer'

readme.text:
Peer-to-peer messaging between DeepSeek Harness **sessions** — a native DSH
take on the Pi `coms` extension.

> npm package: `@jjunho/dsh-peer2peer`

This plugin is a migration of the **`coms`** (and `coms-net`) peer-to-peer
extensions from the [pi-vs-claude-code](https://github.com/jjunho/pi-vs-claude-code)
project. The original idea — two equal agents talking to each other
peer-to-peer instead of through a parent/child hierarchy — comes from there.
Thanks for that work.

The DeepSeek Harness runs many sessions in **one process** (the Web GUI serves
every window as a session of the same runtime). Two "windows" are two sessions
of that process, and they talk to each other directly through an **in-memory
bus** — no sockets, no files, no registry, no tokens, no hub.

> Scope: this plugin connects sessions **of the same DSH process**. Two separate
> `dsh` processes do not share memory, so cross-process peering would need a
> socket or network transport.

- **dsh** installed and on `PATH`.
- **pnpm** on `PATH` — `dsh plugin add` forwards to pnpm.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @jjunho/dsh-peer2peer
```

Then restart the profile for the row to mount:

```sh
dsh --profile web
```

You can also install a local checkout or a fresh clone:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add file:/absolute/path/to/dsh-peer2peer
```

`--profile web` is the Web GUI app; the package works with any profile
(`headless`, a custom profile, etc.).

> **pnpm peer-dependency warning is expected.** The package uses
> `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` and `@deepseek-ai/cordis` from the DSH installation
> itself, so pnpm does not install them — that is correct, do not `pnpm add`
> them into the profile.

1. Start the Web GUI and open **two sessions** (two tabs / windows).
2. In each session, tell the agent to identify itself as a peer:
   - window 1: *"Configure yourself as the `frontend` peer in project `my-app`"*
   - window 2: *"Configure yourself as the `backend` peer in project `my-app`"*

The agent calls `peer_configure(name=..., project=...)` in each window. Peers
   only discover each other within the **same project**.
3. Hand work from one window to the other:
   - window 1: *"Send the backend peer: analyze the API contract and tell me
     which endpoints are missing"* → the agent calls `peer_send`.
   - window 2: **the agent wakes up by itself** — the message is pushed into its
     inbox, it does the work, and answers with `peer_reply`. No one has to type
     anything in window 2.
   - window 1: the agent calls `peer_get` to read the response.

Identity is set **per session** with `peer_configure`, or seeded from
environment variables as defaults:

| Variable            | Meaning                                    | Default                               |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------- |
| `DSH_PEER_NAME`     | Default peer name                          | `agent-<8 hex of session id>`         |
| `DSH_PEER_PROJECT`  | Default shared project                     | current directory basename            |
| `DSH_PEER_PURPOSE`  | Default purpose                            | empty                                 |
| `DSH_PEER_MODEL`    | Model label shown to peers                 | empty                                 |
| `DSH_PEER_CWD`      | Working directory shown to peers           | process cwd                           |

`peer_configure` overrides these per session, so two windows in one process can
have distinct names (`frontend` / `backend`) — something a single process-wide
env var cannot express.

1. `peer_configure(name?, purpose?, project?)` — set this session's identity.
2. `peer_list` — discover peers in the project.
3. `peer_send(target, prompt)` — hand a task to a peer; returns a `msg_id`. The
   peer's live agent is **woken proactively**.
4. `peer_reply(msg_id, response)` — answer an inbound prompt; routed back to the
   sender.
5. `peer_get(msg_id)` — poll the status/response of a message you sent.
6. `peer_await(timeout_ms?)` — fallback poll of the inbox, used only when a peer
   has no live agent to wake (default 30 s).

```
frontend (A)              backend (B)
    │  peer_send(B, "...")     │
    │─────────────────────────▶│  wakes B's agent
    │                          │  ... B works autonomously ...

| Symptom                                       | Fix                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pnpm not found on PATH`                      | Install pnpm; `dsh plugin` needs it.                                                |
| Tools missing after install                   | The profile must be restarted for the new row to mount.                             |
| Peer list is empty despite two sessions       | Same project in both? Both sessions in the **same** process?                        |
| `peer "x" not found`                          | The target has a different name/project, or hasn't called `peer_configure` yet.     |
| pnpm warns "peer dep unmet"                   | Expected — see Install.                                                             |
| Two separate `dsh` processes can't see each other | Expected: the bus is in-memory and scoped to one process (see How it works).   |
